thread.title: The Market Is Healthy - Just Look At All The Recent Buybacks

author: John Buckingham
title: The Market Is Healthy - Just Look At All The Recent Buybacks
text:
A healthier economy, along with the benefits of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, has added to the enthusiasm in executive suites across Corporate America, with management teams stepping up efforts to share the wealth with their stockholders. According to the S&P Dow Jones Indices, companies in the S&P 500-stock index increased repurchases of their own shares by more than 40 percent in the first quarter of 2018, compared with 2017. And judging by recent events, more repurchases are on the way for Q2. Yesterday, MetLife, Inc. (NYSE: MET) announced a new $1.5 billion authorization for the company’s common stock in addition to increasing its quarterly common stock dividend by five percent.
Earlier this month, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) announced it would buy back $100 billion in stock, as well as increase its dividend by a sizable 16 percent to 73 cents a share. Luca Maestri, Apple’s Chief Financial Officer, told the New York Times that “because we’re making all the right investments all around the company, it makes perfect sense for us not to keep the cash on our balance sheet but return it to investors.”
The logo of the American multinational technology company Apple headquartered in Cupertino, California, that designs, develops, and sells consumer electronics, computer software, and online services is seen in the Munich pedestrian zone. (Photo by...
On May 9, wireless technology giant Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) announced a new stock repurchase program for $10 billion of the company's shares.
These recent repurchase authorization announcements merely add to our faith in the long-term prospects of our broadly diversified portfolios of undervalued stocks. And, with:
investor sentiment far from optimistic interest rates still very low by historical standards corporate profits poised to enjoy significant growth this year and next dividend payouts rising the global economies showing modest to moderate growth; and equity valuations far more reasonable after this year’s churning We see plenty of reasons to remain positive on the U.S. and global equity markets.
